content: A Mongolian spot, also known as a Mongolian blue spot, is a benign, flat, congenital birthmark characterized by wavy borders and an irregular shape. It is most commonly observed among individuals of East Asian descent and derives its name from the Mongolian population. This condition is also highly prevalent among East Africans and Native Americans. Typically, these spots fade away within three to five years after birth and almost always disappear by puberty. The Mongolian spot is a congenital developmental condition that exclusively affects the skin. Its blue coloration is caused by melanocytes, which are melanin-containing cells located deep within the dermis. These spots often appear as multiple patches or a single large area, commonly covering regions such as the lumbosacral area (lower back), buttocks, flanks, and shoulders. The condition arises due to the entrapment of melanocytes in the dermis during their migration from the neural crest to the epidermis during embryonic development. It is not associated with sex, as both male and female infants are equally predisposed to developing Mongolian spots. These spots are entirely harmless. However, in individuals unfamiliar with their origin, they may sometimes be mistaken for bruises. Mongolian spots are most prevalent among Mongols and other East Asian populations, including Chinese, Koreans, Japanese, and Vietnamese. Nearly all East Asian infants are born with one or more Mongolian spots, with an incidence rate of 95–100%. The condition is also common when only one parent is of East Asian descent. Among East African infants, the prevalence is approximately 90–95%, while 85–90% of Native American infants are affected. In contrast, the incidence among Caucasians—defined as the indigenous populations of Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and the Indian subcontinent (including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka)—is significantly lower, ranging from 1–10%. Additionally, the prevalence among Hispanics is estimated to be 50–70%, likely due to the Native American genetic admixture present in mestizos, individuals of mixed European and Native American ancestry, who constitute the largest racial group among Hispanics.
